newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan's Hub Power ahead of schedule.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's Hub Power ahead of schedule.

text.p: Pakistan's $1.6 billion Hub power project will be completed ahead of schedule, Hub Power Co Ltd (HUBCO) chief executive Michael Woodroffe said on Monday.

"The whole complex will be completed during February," Woodroffe told reporters, adding that early completion would save about $30 million. The 1,292 megawatt plant had been scheduled for completion by the end of March 1997.
Woodroffe said the third 323-MW generator had taken full load on Sunday and all the machinery for the complex was now at the site, some 40 km (25 miles) northwest of Karachi.
He said state-run Pakistan State Oil would start pumping fuel oil to the complex from Port Qasim next week.
"The cost of running the plant is very low," Woodroffe said, adding that the complex was already generating income that was being used to repay loans and reduce borrowing.

HUBCO, to be operated and maintained by Britain's National Power Plc for 12 years, will charge 5.8 cents per kilowatt hour from the state-run Water and Power Development Authority, the bulk buyer of electricity from the plant.
Woodroffe said HUBCO was likely to pay its first interim dividend in March 1998 and a final one six months later.
HUBCO was set up to design, construct, finance, own and operate the oil-fired power station near the Hub River estuary in the southwestern province of Balochistan.

Construction began under a turnkey contract with a group led by Mitsui & Co Ltd, and including Ishikawajima-Harima Heavy Industries Co Ltd of Japan, Ansaldo Energia S.p.A of Italy and Campenon Bernard SGE of France.
